$meta.name: Vitrine
$meta.description: A frosted-glass SKIN: translucent panes over a dark scene, a vivid spring-green accent, generous radii. Generated into dist/jrk-skin-vitrine.css by scripts/build-tokens.mjs. Never hand-edit dist/.
$meta.$axisNote: THIS IS NOT A THIRD THEME. It carries its own light and dark halves, so it is orthogonal to the theme and is stamped separately: data-skin="vitrine" crossed with data-theme. Four blocks, not one.
$meta.$scopeNote: COLOUR, SHADOW, RADIUS AND TRACKING ONLY. The glass itself — the blur, the scrim, the backdrop hook and the rounded tile list — lives in css/skins/vitrine.css, which holds no colour at all.
$meta.$glassNote: THE ONE THING TO UNDERSTAND BEFORE CHANGING ANYTHING: surface-default is the glass COMPOSITED over the scrim, recorded flat so the gate can measure it. The scrim is not decoration — it is what BOUNDS the composite. Without it a pale backdrop behind a translucent pane composites far lighter than the recorded hex and every ink ratio in this file becomes fiction. Backdrop, scrim, glass alpha and surface-default are one decision in four places.
$meta.$darkNote: DARK IS THE FAITHFUL HALF AND LIGHT IS A DESIGN DECISION, the arrangement midgard records. The reference is a dark scene lit from within; inverting it produces a pale ground under a green that cannot be read on it, which is what the stepped light accent roles exist to avoid.

vars.$comment: Keyed by CSS variable name without the --jrk- prefix. The build asserts every one exists in the base layer; skin-only names go in skinOnly.

surface-canvas.$note: A three-stop cool ramp standing in for the reference photograph. THE SKIN SHIPS NO IMAGE: this library has never shipped a binary, and sync-design.mjs mirrors whole directories into the consuming app, so a photograph would ride along on every sync. A consumer points --jrk-vitrine-backdrop at its own image instead and this ramp is what shows when nothing does. Every ink is held to the ramp's WORST stop, not to the panel.

surface-default.$note: THE COMPOSITED VALUE OF THE GLASS, NOT ITS FILL, and that distinction is the whole architecture of this skin. A frosted tile is translucent, so its ink ground is whatever happens to be behind it — which would void every contrast guarantee in the library. scripts/validate-skin.mjs refuses that outright: it fails with 'surface-default is not a flat colour; every other check measures against it'. So this token records what the glass RESOLVES TO over the scrim and the clamped backdrop, as a flat hex, and the gate goes on measuring all 73 checks against it exactly as it does for an opaque skin. The translucency lives in surface-glass and is used only for rendering. If the glass alpha or the scrim moves, THIS VALUE MUST BE RE-COMPOSITED IN THE SAME COMMIT — it is the one number in the file that is derived from two others and cannot be checked against them.

surface-banner.$note: THE MASTHEAD IS GLASS TOO, so this records the band COMPOSITED over the clamped backdrop and the scrim — the same arrangement surface-default uses for tiles, and for the same reason: validate:skin needs a flat hex to measure against. The band spans #efefef..#fefefe in light and #191f1f..#242a29 in dark whatever the consumer puts behind it, and every banner ink was solved against BOTH ends, not against this recorded middle. Unlike midgard, which turns backdrop-filter off on its bar to get one flat certain plane, this skin leaves it on: a frosted masthead over the scene IS the reference, and the clamp is what makes it safe.

text-muted.$note: SOLVED AGAINST THE COMPOSITE RANGE, NOT THE RECORDED PANEL, and it is the one ink where that distinction bites. On surface-default it measures comfortably; but surface-default is what the glass resolves to over a MID backdrop, and the real ground moves as the consumer's image does. Across the full range the scrim allows, the first value tried landed at 4.46:1 — under by 0.04, and invisible to validate:skin, which only ever sees the flat recorded hex. Held to the pale extreme instead, and to status-neutral-wash, which is the lightest ground any dark ink here sits on.

accent-solid.$note: The vivid spring green of the reference. Vivid in both halves as a FILL; every text role steps away from it in light, because a saturated green on a white panel clears 4.5:1 in none of them. That is the warm-high-chroma-accent finding this library has now recorded three times — industry's yellow, midgard's gold, and now this — so the shape of the rule is confirmed for a COOL high-chroma accent too: it is about chroma against a pale plate, not about hue.

status-neutral-text.$note: RE-STEPPED OFF text-muted, which it otherwise mirrors. Muted clears the panel and the page but lands at 4.00:1 on status-neutral-wash — the neutral wash is the LIGHTEST ground any dark ink sits on in this palette, so it binds where the panel does not. Solved against all three grounds at once.

shadow-card.$note: MAY NEVER BE none. css/skins/vitrine.css composes var(--jrk-shadow-card) into the glass edge, and a box-shadow list containing none is invalid CSS that drops the whole declaration. Same constraint midgard records for the same reason. The inset highlight is the top-edge catch that makes a pane read as glass; on the dark page it is the ONLY thing that reads, because a black shadow over a near-black ground renders nothing — the fourth independent arrival at on a dark ground, elevation is a fill.

shadow-md.$note: MAY NEVER BE none — see shadow-card.

shadow-focus.$note: TWO-TONE IN BOTH HALVES, and gated as such for every skin. A single-tone ring in the accent is invisible against a pale panel, and the ring is the library's one focus indicator.

radius-lg.$note: ROUNDED IS THIS SKIN'S SIGNATURE, the inverse of both existing skins. industry and midgard each square a NAMED LIST of controls; vitrine rounds a named list of TILES in css/skins/vitrine.css. Note the base library reaches for radius.none directly on tiles rather than radius-lg, so overriding this token alone rounds nothing — the stylesheet has to name the tiles. Anything new that wants the glass treatment stays square until it is added there.

skinOnly.$comment: Names with no base counterpart, exempt from the build exists-in-base assertion. Every one is referenced from css/skins/vitrine.css — validate:skin FAILS on a skinOnly token nothing draws.

vitrine-backdrop.$note: THE DEFAULT BACKDROP, AND IT HAS TO HAVE STRUCTURE OR THE SKIN IS NOT FROSTED. backdrop-filter blurs WHAT IS BEHIND THE ELEMENT: over a flat fill it returns the same flat fill and the blur is a no-op. The first version of this skin defaulted to none and shipped a pane with nothing behind it — measurably correct, and visibly not glass. So the default is a scene: two coloured pools, a dim floor wash, and a fine diagonal rule at 54px. THE RULE IS THE PART THAT READS — a gradient blurs to almost itself, but repeating hairlines smear into soft bands, which is what a viewer recognises as frosting. A consumer replaces this wholesale with their own url(); anything they supply is bounded by vitrine-clamp before it reaches the glass.

vitrine-scrim.$note: A TINT NOW, NOT A VEIL. With vitrine-clamp doing the bounding, the scrim only has to carry the palette cast — so it dropped from 0.94 to 0.30 and 75% of the backdrop reaches the glass. It is still measured as part of the composite; it is no longer what makes the composite safe.

surface-glass.$note: HALF-TRANSPARENT, where the first version was 0.70/0.72 and read as a tinted rectangle. Every ink was solved against the PALE EXTREME of the composite this produces over the clamped backdrop, not against the recorded surface-default: dark spans #141918..#222726, light spans #e8e9e9..#fdfefe.

surface-glass-raised.$note: Overlays sit closer to the reader and take a denser pane, so a menu over a card still reads as in front of it rather than merged with it.

vitrine-clamp.$note: THE BOUND, AND IT REPLACED A NEARLY-OPAQUE SCRIM. The first version bounded the backdrop by COVERAGE — a 0.94-alpha veil — which made every ratio true and destroyed the effect, because 6% of an image is nothing to blur. This bounds it by LUMINANCE instead: any image a consumer supplies is compressed into #101010..#373737 in dark and #c1c1c1..#ffffff in light, so the composite stays measurable while the image keeps its STRUCTURE, which is what the blur needs. THE FILTER ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: CSS applies filters in the order listed, and contrast() pulls toward mid-grey while brightness() scales. contrast-then-brightness lands a dark band; brightness-then-contrast lifts blacks to grey and the bound is lost. Do not reorder.

masthead-fill.$note: An indirection, not a new colour — the same denser pane overlays use, so the bar reads as the topmost plane. Kept as its own name so a future change to the masthead does not repaint every menu and modal with it.

masthead-ink.$note: One variable re-inks the whole interior of the bar — captions, statuses, ghost buttons, the search field — because base pipes all of them through gradient-ink.
